headline_marked: Hackers claim [[19m Pathao users' data leaked]], demand $400,000
headline: Hackers claim 19m Pathao users' data leaked, demand $400,000
summary: A hacker group claims to have stolen 133GB of data, including NIDs and addresses, demanding a ransom to prevent its release.
details: A hacker group claims to have accessed the personal data of approximately 19 million Pathao users. The stolen information allegedly includes phone numbers, emails, NIDs, driving licenses, locations, Facebook identities, and home addresses.

The attackers are demanding $400,000 from Pathao to prevent the release of the data. According to the cyber security platform Daily Dark Web, the claim was posted on the dark web and shared on X (formerly Twitter).

Pathao confirmed in a statement that some personal information, including names, email addresses, and phone numbers, was accessed by miscreants. The company stated that the incident was brought under control immediately after detection.
On October 4, Pathao experienced temporary service disruptions. As a precautionary measure, the company took its critical systems offline to secure information and protect the platform.
The hackers claim to possess 133GB of data containing 250 million records across 591 databases. The largest database allegedly contains information for 19,063,918 accounts.
Beyond user data, the group claims to have stolen internal business information, including employee records, administrative access logs, merchant bank accounts, and transaction details.

Cyber security expert Tanveer Hassan Zoha suggested that Pathao should conduct an independent digital forensic investigation and preserve all digital evidence, including access logs and servers, while notifying regulatory authorities.
caption:

Pathao confirmed in a statement that some personal information, including names, email addresses, and phone numbers, was accessed by miscreants. The company stated that the incident was brought under control immediately after detection.

On October 4, Pathao experienced temporary service disruptions. As a precautionary measure, the company took its critical systems offline to secure information and protect the platform.

The hackers claim to possess 133GB of data containing 250 million records across 591 databases. The largest database allegedly contains information for 19,063,918 accounts.

Beyond user data, the group claims to have stolen internal business information, including employee records, administrative access logs, merchant bank accounts, and transaction details.

headline_marked: DP World to [[operate Chittagong's New Mooring Container Terminal]] for 15 years
headline: DP World to operate Chittagong's New Mooring Container Terminal for 15 years
summary: The deal includes a 1,000 crore BDT investment for modernization and a 600 crore BDT advance fee for the port authority.
details: The Chittagong Port Authority has signed a 15-year agreement with Dubai-based DP World to operate the New Mooring Container Terminal (NCT), the largest terminal at the port.
The agreement, signed at the Invest Bangladesh office in Dhaka, is a government-to-government (G2G) deal based on a public-private partnership (PPP) model.
DP World will invest over 1,000 crore BDT in modernization, equipment, and technology over the first 10 years of the operation.
The port authority will receive an advance fee of approximately 600 crore BDT, with 25% paid upon signing and the remaining 75% before operations begin.
Under the revenue-sharing model, the Chittagong Port will receive between 40% and 67% of the average revenue from container operations.
The deal was signed amid protests from leftist organizations and port workers, who argue that the NCT is a profitable terminal and should not be leased to a foreign operator.
Police used batons to disperse protesters outside the signing ceremony in Dhaka, while further demonstrations occurred in Chittagong.
The terminal will be fully handed over to DP World within the next six months, following the fulfillment of several essential conditions including environmental clearances.
caption:
A 1,000 crore BDT investment for modernization, but protests erupt as DP World takes over Chittagong's largest container terminal.

The Chittagong Port Authority has signed a 15-year agreement with Dubai-based DP World to operate the New Mooring Container Terminal (NCT), the largest terminal at the port.

The agreement, signed at the Invest Bangladesh office in Dhaka, is a government-to-government (G2G) deal based on a public-private partnership (PPP) model.

DP World will invest over 1,000 crore BDT in modernization, equipment, and technology over the first 10 years of the operation.

The port authority will receive an advance fee of approximately 600 crore BDT, with 25% paid upon signing and the remaining 75% before operations begin.

Under the revenue-sharing model, the Chittagong Port will receive between 40% and 67% of the average revenue from container operations.

The deal was signed amid protests from leftist organizations and port workers, who argue that the NCT is a profitable terminal and should not be leased to a foreign operator.

Police used batons to disperse protesters outside the signing ceremony in Dhaka, while further demonstrations occurred in Chittagong.

The terminal will be fully handed over to DP World within the next six months, following the fulfillment of several essential conditions including environmental clearances.
